data: Japan's heavy-lift gateway — H-IIA + H3, HTV / HTV-X cargo to the ISS

Yoshinobu Launch Complex at the Tanegashima Space Center on Japan's southern island. Original H-II first flight August 1996; H-IIA from 2001 (a workhorse with a 49-out-of-50 success rate); HTV cargo to the ISS from 2009 to 2020; HTV-X from 2025 onward. LP-1 was upgraded for the new H3 in 2023. Tanegashima's 30°N latitude is workable for geostationary launches with the southern Pacific corridor downrange. Coordinates from JAXA fact sheets.

On Tanegashima, the southern Japanese island that's been home to JAXA's orbital programme since 1969. LP-1 hosted the H-II maiden flight in 1996; the H-IIA from 2001 (49 successes in 50 flights; retired June 2025 after its final mission); the seven HTV cargo flights to the ISS between 2009 and 2020; and from 2023 the new H3 rocket. Tanegashima's 30°N geometry is workable for geostationary launches — the south Pacific is empty downrange — and the fishing fleet stand-down windows are famously short, giving Japan some of the tightest launch-window protocols in the world.
